title: Wren and the Choir
premise: Coral Underhill has survived seven years in the city of Vell by stealing memories and selling them as charms, hiding the fact that they are one of the last living conduits of the outlawed Choir-magic. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out, Coral learns the truth: the country of Ashenmoor was never real — it is a memory, stolen whole from the world by the Choir's founders to hide a dying god, and now that memory is unraveling. Hunted by the Warden who once trained them and bound to a ragtag found family of smugglers, exiles, and a runaway priest named Sable Fen, Coral must reach the Door at the heart of the unraveling land — the only way back into the real world. In the end, Coral chooses to give up their own stolen memories, including every moment with Sable, to sing the country closed and let its people pass through; the book closes with Sable finding Coral alive but unremembering, choosing to stay beside them and begin again.
about_author: Marguerite Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed, an experience she describes as 'stealing memories legally.' She writes fantasy about people who survive by taking what others discard, and lives in a coastal town where the fog arrives like a debt collector.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A night of ordinary theft: Coral lifts a widow's memory of her wedding day and sells it as a luck-charm in Vell's night market. Establishes their rules, their loneliness, and the ache of carrying other people's best moments. Emotional beat: competence masking emptiness.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with flashbacks. We learn how Coral fled the Choir's conservatory seven years ago after refusing a Rite, and how the city's anti-magic wards both protect and suffocate them. They almost sell a memory of their own mother. Emotional beat: the cost of staying hidden.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Sold Rain
chapters.summary: Coral meets Pip, a feral child street-thief who claims he can bottle weather. Coral takes him in half-reluctantly, the first crack in their solitude. Meanwhile, the city's wardens post notices: magic crimes will now mean the Gleaning. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: Sable Fen Sings in the Dark
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A disgraced priest of the dead Choir performs forbidden hymns in a flooded crypt for coin. He recognizes Coral in his audience — not their face, but the resonance of their voice. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's true names.

chapters.title: What the Stars Did Not Do
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The stars go out, all at once, like snuffed candles. Panic in Vell; the wardens blame sorcery. Coral feels their stolen memories stirring, whispering coordinates. Emotional beat: dread dressed as wonder.

chapters.title: The Night the Border Fell
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The border wards shatter; beyond the walls, the countryside simply isn't there — gray static where fields should be. Refugees pour in claiming villages have 'forgotten themselves.' Coral realizes the whispers in their head are map-fragments. Emotional beat: the hidden life ends.

chapters.title: Warden Halloway
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. The Warden who trained Coral before their defection arrives in Vell, tasked with finding whoever can still hear the Choir. Flashbacks reveal Halloway loved Coral once, and reported them anyway. Emotional beat: love curdled into duty.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Memories
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. To buy passage out of Vell, Coral sells a memory to crime-lord Mother Quill — and accidentally shows her a glimpse of the Door. Quill wants more. Pip overhears. Emotional beat: the past pricing the future.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Oath
chapters.summary: Sable introduces Coral to his crew: Brannoc the ferryman, twins Isolde and Maren who navigate by dead stars, and old Tansy who remembers a country that no longer exists. They agree to carry Coral toward the Door. Emotional beat: a family assembling from wreckage.

chapters.title: Leaving Vell
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The crew slips the city through the drowned sewers as Halloway's wardens close in. Coral must use forbidden magic to hold a collapsing gate open, revealing themselves. Pip stows away. Emotional beat: burning the bridge behind you.

chapters.title: The Gray Country
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Outside, the land is unfinished — roads end mid-stride, forests are sketches of themselves. The crew follows Coral's memory-whispers toward the first Waystation. Emotional beat: awe and terror walking hand in hand.

chapters.title: Villages That Forgot Their Names
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They find a town whose people smile blankly, unable to recall anything older than the starless night. Coral restores one woman's memory and learns the truth: Ashenmoor was stolen from the world long ago. Emotional beat: horror as revelation.

chapters.title: Tansy's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Tansy's POV. The old woman reveals she was born outside the stolen country — she is a stranger here, aging wrong, kept alive only because the land hasn't noticed her yet. She knows the Door needs a Conduit to open. Emotional beat: exile inside exile.

chapters.title: Halloway Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. The Warden captures Mother Quill and learns of the Door. Halloway believes opening it will destroy everyone inside the memory-country; duty demands stopping Coral at any cost. Emotional beat: conviction as tragedy.

chapters.title: The First Waystation
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At a shrine-station, Coral sings a fragment of the Choir and the land briefly remembers itself — green, warm, starred. The crew sees what could be saved. Sable and Coral admit what's growing between them. Emotional beat: hope as temptation.

chapters.title: Pip's Bargain
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Feeling useless, Pip trades a bottled storm to a gray-market ghost for information: the Door lies beneath the Conservatory where Coral was raised. Pip hides this from Coral. Emotional beat: a child learning secrets have weight.

chapters.title: The Choir's True History
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In ruined archives, Sable deciphers that the founders stole the country to imprison a dying god whose death-scream would unmake the world — the stars going out means the god is waking. Emotional beat: faith shattered into understanding.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Wardens attack the crew crossing a river of static. Maren is badly hurt holding the line; Coral uses conduit-magic openly for the first time, saving her but confirming Halloway's fears. Emotional beat: family forged under fire.

chapters.title: What Coral Stole
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, recovering. Maren confronts Coral: she saw inside their magic — Coral has been hoarding thousands of stolen memories, including pieces of the god's own mind. Trust fractures. Emotional beat: the thief caught in their own theft.

chapters.title: The Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The long winter falls early and hard; the unraveling accelerates, erasing whole regions nightly. The crew shelters in a barn and shares stories of home — real homes, some outside the stolen land. Emotional beat: warmth against the dark.

chapters.title: Halloway's Offer
chapters.summary: Halloway corners Coral alone. She offers pardon and restoration if Coral surrenders and lets the country fade peacefully — she believes the god must die quietly. Coral refuses: the people are real, whatever the land is. Emotional beat: two loves, irreconcilable.

chapters.title: The Ghost Market
chapters.summary: Full-cast chapter. The crew trades through a market of the半-forgotten, buying passage and supplies. Coral secretly buys back the wedding-memory they sold in chapter 1 and returns it to the widow's daughter, found among refugees. Emotional beat: restitution.

chapters.title: Sable's Confession
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable admits he was the priest who testified against Coral at the Conservatory years ago — his hymn-recognition in chapter 4 was guilt, not coincidence. Coral walks into the snow. Emotional beat: betrayal by honesty.

chapters.title: Alone in the White Silence
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Wandering alone, Coral hears the god directly for the first time: not monstrous, but terrified, a child-god drowning in its own prison. It begs not to be remembered or forgotten, but freed. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster.

chapters.title: The Twins' Choice
chapters.summary: Isolde and Maren's alternating POV. With Maren maimed, the twins consider abandoning the quest to shelter for winter. Tansy's quiet courage — she is visibly fading, the land finally noticing her — shames them into staying. Emotional beat: chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in the Ruin-Chapel
chapters.summary: Coral and Sable, forced together in a chapel, speak plainly: about the testimony, about fear, about love against every duty either of them owes. They do not fully forgive; they choose to continue anyway. Emotional beat: love as decision, not feeling.

chapters.title: The Conservatory Gates
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The crew reaches the Conservatory where Coral was trained — impossibly intact amid the ruin, maintained by the god's dreaming. Coral faces the corridors of their childhood. Emotional beat: returning to the scene of the wound.

chapters.title: Lessons in the Dark
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, Coral's POV. Inside, Coral relives stored memories: their mother's face, the Rite they refused, the friend they abandoned during their escape. Pip's secret about the Door's location surfaces here. Emotional beat: grief as curriculum.

chapters.title: Mother Quill's Army
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Quill, having sold the Door's location to desperate factions, arrives with mercenaries wanting to seize the Door for power. Three-way standoff with Halloway's wardens outside the gates. Emotional beat: greed arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Conservatory
chapters.summary: Full-cast action chapter. Wardens, mercenaries, and the crew collide as the land unravels around the battlefield. Tansy sacrifices herself to seal a breach, dissolving into remembered light. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Tansy's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Tansy's final POV, dying. She passes Coral her outsider's memory of the real world — grass, oceans, an unbroken sky — the key that lets a Conduit open the Door without being consumed. Emotional beat: inheritance.

chapters.title: Halloway Breaks
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Seeing Tansy's sacrifice and the god's terror through Coral's shared memory, Halloway's certainty collapses. She turns her wardens to hold off Quill's mercenaries instead. Emotional beat: duty bending toward mercy.

chapters.title: Descent to the Door
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The crew descends beneath the Conservatory into the god's prison-heart: a chamber of suspended memories, the dimmed stars hanging like lanterns. Quill pursues. Emotional beat: the quiet before the choice.

chapters.title: Quill's Hubris
chapters.summary: Mother Quill seizes the Door and tries to force it open for conquest; the god's raw memory floods her mind and unmakes her. Her mercenaries flee. Pip saves Coral from the backlash. Emotional beat: ambition meeting consequence.

chapters.title: The God Who Wanted Out
chapters.summary: Coral speaks with the child-god face to face. It cannot leave without destroying everything inside the stolen country — but it can be sung to rest if someone pays with memories of equal weight. Coral understands the price. Emotional beat: terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The Door opens; the people of Ashenmoor can pass into the real world, but only while the god sleeps, and only if a Conduit feeds it their entire remembered life. Coral says goodbye to the crew without telling them the cost. Emotional beat: love disguised as farewell.

chapters.title: The Last Song
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs as Coral sings the Choir complete, feeding the god every memory they own — Vell, Sable, Pip, their mother, their name. The stars reignite over the departing crowds. Sable realizes too late what Coral is doing. Emotional beat: climax, sacrifice, silence.

chapters.title: Through the Door
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The survivors emerge into the real world at dawn. Sable finds Coral collapsed at the threshold: alive, emptied, not knowing him. Halloway vouches for them both. Pip refuses to leave Coral's side. Emotional beat: grief and relief entwined.

chapters.title: The Unremembering
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, fragmented. Coral wakes in a refugee camp by a real sea, holding a charm they don't remember making — containing one memory the god returned as mercy: a single evening, Sable singing in the dark. Emotional beat: a seed left in ash.

chapters.title: Begin Again
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Spring. Sable doesn't demand the old Coral back; he introduces himself as a stranger and asks Coral to sing with him. Pip narrates their new household. Some things, the book argues, can be relearned rather than restored. Emotional beat: found family, chosen twice.
